players.product: power transformers and grid equipment buyer — US utility (largest HD Hyundai Electric customer)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results: CEO said adjusted earnings per share increased by 10% year-over-year, reflecting performance at both FPL and Energy Resources. CFO: FPL earnings per share increased $0.06 year-over-year, driven by regulatory capital growth of approximately 8.8%; Energy Resources reported adjusted earnings growth of approximately 14% year-over-year (new investments +$0.04 per share, NextEra Energy Transmission +$0.05 per share from the sale of a 50% equity interest in a California transmission asset, customer supply -$0.04 per share). FPL Q1 retail sales rose approximately 3.4% year-over-year (roughly 0.3% weather normalized) as customers grew by nearly 100,000.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted EPS +10% YoY; FPL EPS +$0.06; Energy Resources adjusted earnings approximately 14% YoY; FPL retail sales approximately 3.4%

quarterly_data.signal: FPL capital plan: FPL capital expenditures were approximately $3.2 billion for the quarter and full-year 2026 FPL capital investments are expected to be between $12 billion and $13 billion; FPL expects to invest between $90 billion and $100 billion through 2032. CFO said part of the capex pull-in reflects bringing in secured solar supply now at locked-in prices to remove trade impacts. FPL's 10-year site plan shows roughly 4 GW of new gas-fired generation, over 12 GW of solar and over 7 GW of storage; FPL placed approximately 600 MW of new solar in service in Q1 (owned solar portfolio over 8.5 GW). Every gigawatt of large load under FPL's tariff is initially expected to equal roughly $2 billion of CapEx; of about 21 GW of large load interest, a portion of the 12 GW in advanced discussions could be served as soon as 2028, and at least one large load customer is expected to sign by year-end (CFO: no gigawatt amount has been stated).
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 FPL capex approximately $3.2 billion; FY2026 FPL capex $12 billion to $13 billion; $90 billion to $100 billion through 2032; roughly $2 billion of CapEx per GW of large load; first large load service as soon as 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Energy Resources had a record quarter, adding 4 GW of new long-term contracted renewables and storage to backlog, including 1.3 GW of battery storage origination. Backlog now totals approximately 33 GW after 0.3 GW placed in service. CFO: "Roughly 30% of our backlog additions are driven by hyperscalers, while the remaining 70% comes from power utility customers, including cooperatives and municipalities." Energy Resources CEO Brian Bolster said the additions reflect fundamental demand rather than acceleration ahead of tax-credit roll-offs, and that the company has not yet stepped into that acceleration ("We'll probably see that as we start to move out here in the coming quarters").
quarterly_data.figure: 4 GW added to backlog (record), 1.3 GW battery storage; backlog approximately 33 GW; roughly 30% of additions from hyperscalers, 70% from utilities

quarterly_data.signal: Equipment supply as of this call (point in time): solar panels secured through 2029, competitively priced domestic battery storage supply secured through 2029, key wind components secured domestically for new build expectations through 2027, and sufficient transformer capacity to support the build forecast through the end of the decade. On the U.S.-Japan gas projects, CEO: "we'll have ample supply of turbines" (no turbine OEM named).
quarterly_data.figure: solar panels through 2029; battery storage through 2029; wind components through 2027; transformer capacity through the end of the decade

quarterly_data.signal: The U.S. Department of Commerce selected Energy Resources to build 9.5 GW of new gas-fired generation to serve large loads, tied to Japan's $550 billion investment commitment under the U.S.-Japan trade deal: two projects (Texas and Pennsylvania), owned by the U.S. and Japan, developed, built and operated by Energy Resources. Definitive agreements were expected to be completed in the next two-three-month period, with payments tied to milestones. CFO: a capital light investment, "essentially zero capital for us", with potential fee streams covering development, construction and ongoing O&M through the duration of the asset. The Anderson County, Texas site benefits from gas supply via partner Comstock Resources.
quarterly_data.figure: 9.5 GW of gas-fired generation; Japan's $550 billion investment commitment; definitive agreements targeted in the next two-three-month period; essentially zero capital

quarterly_data.signal: Data center hub strategy: over 30 hubs with a year-end goal of roughly 40, feeding a base case of 15 GW of new generation for large load by 2035 (upside 30 GW or more), approximately 50% from gas-fired generation. Four origination channels, each with a named example: hyperscalers directly (collaboration with Google to recommission Duane Arnold), investor-owned utilities (a joint development agreement signed with Xcel earlier this week to jointly plan and deploy generation, storage and transmission for data center demand across Xcel's eight-state service territory), co-ops/municipalities (plan with Basin Electric to develop a 1.5 GW combined cycle plant in North Dakota), and the federal government. CEO: "We're looking at building 2 GW-5 GW for hyperscalers" rather than 200 MW or 300 MW, with many hub discussions starting behind the meter particularly in areas of the country where the load interconnect process is taking five to seven years.
quarterly_data.figure: over 30 hubs, goal roughly 40; 15 GW by 2035 base case, 30 GW upside; approximately 50% gas; Basin Electric 1.5 GW combined cycle; building 2 GW-5 GW for hyperscalers

quarterly_data.signal: Nuclear: the NRC approved the license transfer of the 30% Duane Arnold stake from Central Iowa Power Cooperative and Corn Belt Power Cooperative, clearing the way to full ownership; the plant remains on track to reenter service no later than Q1 2029. On new nuclear, CEO said NextEra would be more inclined to try an SMR at Turkey Point (where units six and seven already hold licenses) rather than an AP1000, would not join a utility consortium, and favors Gen-3 SMR technology over Gen-4 (citing HALEU fuel risk). It is working with SMR OEMs and hyperscalers, including a national collaboration with Google around advanced nuclear, and any project needs the 'four wallets' (OEM, developer, hyperscaler, federal government) for risk sharing.
quarterly_data.figure: 30% Duane Arnold stake transfer approved by NRC; restart no later than Q1 2029; 6 GW of SMR co-location opportunities; Gen-3 SMR focus

quarterly_data.signal: Recontracting: in Q1 NextEra contracted over 600 MW of existing projects, locking in contracts for an average of over 18 years; CEO said pricing on the new contracts is roughly a $20 per megawatt hour average increase relative to prior realized pricing, reflecting the strong electricity demand environment.
quarterly_data.figure: over 600 MW recontracted; average of over 18 years; roughly a $20 per megawatt hour increase

quarterly_data.signal: AI-related partnerships: a collaboration with NVIDIA announced in Q1 to make Bring Your Own Generation data center power flexible, temporarily cycling down or shifting data center activity during extreme heat or cold so the power can serve grid demand ("data centers as giant batteries"). Separately, the Rewire initiative with Google Cloud is an enterprise-wide AI transformation and AI product development platform; first Rewire products brought to market in Q1 include Conduit, Generation Entitlement and Grid Composer, which NextEra and Google are delivering to the utility industry.

Gas build-out constraint: CEO said the biggest constraint on building gas generation faster is labor at EPC contractors: the industry once had nine, 10, 11 EPC contractors building gas plants, versus the four EPC contractors NextEra does business with today, and those firms are also building LNG terminals and data centers. Permitting is the other gating factor. He added that manufacturing has started to ramp and EPC labor is responding.
quarterly_data.figure: four EPC contractors today vs nine, 10, 11 historically

quarterly_data.signal: Transmission and pipelines: Lone Star Transmission received ERCOT approval to build portions of two new North Central Texas lines, an investment share of approximately $300 million (roughly 40% increase in Lone Star's rate base). NextEra Energy Transmission has secured more than $5 billion in new projects since 2023 and has $8 billion of regulated and secured capital. The combined electric and gas transmission business at Energy Resources is expected to reach $20 billion of regulated and investment capital by 2032, a 20% compound annual growth rate off a 2025 base. The Q1 acquisition of Symmetry Energy Solutions brings total gas transported and delivered to approximately 2.9 trillion cu ft annually.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $300 million Lone Star investment; more than $5 billion since 2023; $8 billion regulated and secured capital; $20 billion by 2032 (20% CAGR)

connects_to.relationship: power for Google data centers — collaboration to recommission NextEra's Duane Arnold nuclear plant (cited as the example of NextEra's channel of working directly with hyperscalers to power their data centers)

contracts.signal: CEO: "The first channel is working directly with hyperscalers to power their data centers... A great example is our collaboration with Google to recommission our Duane Arnold nuclear plant outside Cedar Rapids, Iowa." The plant remains on track to reenter service no later than Q1 2029. CEO also cited "our national collaboration with Google, for example, around advanced nuclear. We're looking together with Google at where that might make the most sense."
contracts.type: nuclear power supply / plant recommissioning collaboration
